I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I am p2 with $1045 and only one opponent remains. I own four mortgaged properties: Vermont, Connecticut, States, and St. James Place.

I also own hotels on Kentucky, Indiana, and Illinois, plus a hotel on Boardwalk. My opponent owns a brown monopoly with hotels on Mediterranean and Baltic, plus several mortgaged properties.

The opponent is on B&O Railroad with $223 cash. I will end the turn.

Trading would be dangerous. Completing their light blue, pink, or green monopolies would strengthen them too much.

I am on Reading Railroad, so I will not land on the opponent's brown hotels until I complete another lap.

A roll of 12 from B&O Railroad lands on Park Place, which would cost the opponent roughly $1500. Boardwalk is unreachable this turn. This confirms ending the turn is the right move.

Unmortgaging all three orange properties would cost roughly $308. The resulting hotel rent would be about $2500 total, which exceeds the opponent's liquidity of roughly $683. This confirms that unmortgaging is not worthwhile.
